## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Keep all original vertices, including isolates. Let C be the endpoints of any maximal matching and put I = V(G) \ C. Then |C| ≤ 2k and I is independent: every cover meets each matching edge, and an edge entirely outside C would contradict maximality. This is polynomial-time decomposition, with no decision kernel. Handle ℓ < 0 or ℓ > |C|+1 as count zero, and ℓ = 0 as count one.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O(k^2)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. Let Q_j(H) be the number of j-vertex cliques in H, with Q_0(H)=1 and Q_j(H)=0 when j<0 or j>|V(H)|. Since a clique uses at most one vertex outside C, $Q_\ell(G)=Q_\ell(G[C])+\sum_{v\in I}Q_{\ell-1}(G[C\cap N(v)])$.

2. These cases are disjoint. A clique entirely in C belongs to the first term; every other clique has exactly one outside vertex v, which determines its term uniquely. No outside-extension multiplicity is discarded: each possible outside vertex is represented by its own summand.

3. For each term on a vertex set B, use one bit x_u per u in B and impose $\neg x_u\vee\neg x_v$ for each nonedge uv of G[B]. Add $\sum_{u\in B}x_u=j$ with the linear-size adder from [METHODS.md, Section 2](../../METHODS.md), using full equivalences for every gate and fixing the sum bits to j. Handle empty B and impossible j directly.

4. Each j-clique of G[B] determines one input assignment and exactly one extension to all sum and carry variables. Thus #SAT returns exactly Q_j(G[B]). Each query has N = O(k), M = O(k²), and width at most three, including all auxiliary variables.

5. For a specified ℓ, at most n+1 counting calls suffice, where n is the original number of vertices. Add their integer answers. Every answer and their sum have at most n+1 bits because the number of cliques is at most 2^n, so this arithmetic is polynomial in the input length L.

6. The whole size distribution, and hence the total number of cliques including the empty clique, can also be obtained by repeating for ℓ = 0,...,|C|+1. This uses O((n+1)(k+2)) calls; all larger sizes have count zero. The specified-size algorithm and this optional extension both satisfy the displayed conditional A(k) bound with polynomial space when calls are executed sequentially.

7. The decomposition and counting bijection are self-contained catalog deductions. The argument uses the original vertices throughout and does not infer preservation of counts from a decision kernel.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The parameter is the vertex cover number k, not ℓ. An optimum vertex cover need not be supplied or computed.
- A nonminimal computed cover does not cause double counting: the fixed partition C,I determines a unique case for each clique.
- Isolated vertices contribute their singleton cliques through the outside-vertex summands. The empty clique occurs only in the size-zero first term.
- Per-query clause counts can be quadratic in k, so the general-density A(k) profile is used. Full gate equivalences, not mere equisatisfiability, justify the counting step.

Counting requires a count-preserving encoding and preprocessing, or an explicit correction for multiplicities. The derivation must justify this; decision preservation alone is insufficient.
